fixes.explanation: The verse never brings up wages. The LORD says, "A son honors his father, and a servant his master." Wages aren't in that line at all. The thing in view is honor.

Gifts are a nice guess, since the priests are offering things at an altar. But in this verse the LORD names honor, not gifts: "A son honors his father, and a servant his master." Then He asks, "…where is My honor?" Honor is the word here, and the offerings come up in the verses after.
Defiled is right. The LORD says they present "…defiled food on My altar." Then the priests ask, "How have we defiled You?" and He answers that they say the table of the LORD is contemptible.
Borrowed isn't in the verse. The LORD says the priests present defiled food on His altar. What He names here is the condition of the food.

True. The LORD says, "Try offering them to your governor!" Then He asks, "Would he be pleased with you or show you favor?" It's like showing up to your boss's party with a busted lamp and calling it a gift.
The LORD really does say it. After naming the blind, lame and sick animals, He says, "Try offering them to your governor!" Then He asks, "Would he be pleased with you or show you favor?"
That's it. The LORD says, "…you turn up your nose at it…" That's how the priests treat the LORD's table.
Weeping isn't mentioned in these verses. The LORD says they say, "Oh, what a nuisance!" and "…you turn up your nose at it…" I think that sounds like complaining and contempt, not sorrow.
A defective animal is right. The man has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it. Then he "…sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord." The LORD calls that man a deceiver.
Wild animals don't show up in the verse. The man has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it. What he actually sacrifices is a defective animal. That's the word the text uses.
Blessings is right. The LORD says, "I will send a curse among you, and I will curse your blessings." That's a serious one. Their blessings are named right there in the curse.

The text says otherwise. The LORD says, "Yes, I have already begun to curse them, because you are not taking it to heart." It's already begun. The "if" at the start of this same verse doesn't change that.
That's right. The LORD says the covenant "…called for reverence, and he revered Me and stood in awe of My name." Levi answered the covenant with reverence. That is what it called for.
That's not what the text says about Levi. The LORD says of him, "…he revered Me and stood in awe of My name." Levi answered the covenant with reverence. The text doesn't mention him growing weary.

That's it. The LORD says, "…people should seek instruction from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts." That's the reason the verse gives. The priest is called the messenger of the LORD of Hosts.

Stumble is right. The LORD says, "…you have departed from the way, and your instruction has caused many to stumble." Two things are named there. The priests departed from the way, and their instruction caused many to stumble.

Boast isn't the word. The LORD says, "…your instruction has caused many to stumble." It's about stumbling, not bragging. He says the priests departed from the way, and the stumbling is what their instruction caused.

Partiality is right. The LORD says they "…have not kept My ways, but have shown partiality in matters of the law." In matters of the law, they showed partiality. That's a long way from Levi, of whom the LORD says, "…nothing false was found on his lips."
